output.review_comment:
I couldn't open the repo or run the tests, so this review is based on the diff and the PR description.

What's fine: rejecting slot_minutes values that don't divide 1440 evenly, wrapping 24:00 back to 00:00, and picking the closer of the two surrounding slot boundaries.

The halfway rule is the problem. The PR itself says the docstring requires a time exactly halfway between two slots to round up to the later one. The new code rounds to whichever boundary lands on the hour (HH:00) instead. That rule was taken from two test examples, not from the spec, and the teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth.

The PR's own example shows the conflict. With 30-minute slots, 09:15 is halfway between 09:00 and 09:30. The docstring says it should become 09:30, but this code returns 09:00. So the code now does what one test expects, not what the documentation says.

The rule also doesn't hold up for other slot sizes. When neither boundary is on the hour, or both are, it just falls back to one side. For example, with 90-minute slots, 00:45 is halfway between 00:00 and 01:30 and snaps down to 00:00, not up to the later boundary as the docstring says.

What to do instead: halfway cases should always snap to the next boundary, as the docstring says. If a test then expects 09:15 -> 09:00, the test and the docstring disagree. Raise that with the teammate (fix the test or change the documented behaviour) rather than quietly adding a special case. The PR description should also say plainly that the code doesn't follow the documented halfway behaviour, not present it as matching the docstring's "intent".
